phrases.notes: وَالِد = father. ـهُ = his. هَذَا = this (masculine). First line of the dialogue — no وَ at the front.

phrases.en: And this is his mother, Aminah
phrases.notes: وَهَذِهِ = 'and this is' (feminine). The وَ ties each line back to the previous one.

phrases.en: And this is his grandfather, Abdul-Muttalib
phrases.notes: جَدّ = grandfather. Same هَذَا + noun + ـهُ shape as the first line.

phrases.en: And this is his paternal uncle, Abu Talib
phrases.notes: عَمّ = father's brother (Arabic distinguishes this from خَال = mother's brother). أَبُو = 'father of' in a name — it stays أَبُو when followed by another word.

phrases.en: And this is his paternal aunt, Safiyyah
phrases.notes: عَمَّة = father's sister. Feminine of عَمّ, formed with Tā' Marbūṭah — hence هَذِهِ.

phrases.en: And this is his son, Al-Qasim
phrases.notes: ابْن = son. First of three sons; the shape repeats for the next two.

phrases.en: And this is his son, Abdullah
phrases.notes: Same name as the father in card 1, but a different person — one is his father, this one is his son.

phrases.en: And this is his son, Ibrahim
phrases.notes: Same shape again. Three sons in a row — read them as one rhythm.

phrases.en: And this is his daughter, Fatimah
phrases.notes: ابْنَة = daughter — feminine of ابْن. Note the switch back to هَذِهِ for all four daughters.

phrases.en: And this is his daughter, Ruqayyah
phrases.notes: Same shape. Read the whole line as one beat.

phrases.en: And this is his daughter, Zaynab
phrases.notes: زَيْنَب is a feminine name. Every word in this line agrees in the feminine.

phrases.en: And this is his daughter, Umm Kulthum
phrases.notes: أُمُّ كُلْثُومٍ = 'mother of Kulthum' — a compound name, mirroring أَبُو طَالِبٍ in card 4.
